full_findings.text: Demographics: female patient in her early 50s
Chief complaint: multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
Number of lesions: approximately 10
Lesion characteristics: bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules
Lesion location: lower legs
Lesion growth: very slow in number and size since age 24
Lesion bleeding: occasional after trauma
Mobility aid: wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Cause of hemiparesis and hemianopsia: intracranial hemorrhage
History of seizures: recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema: present in the lower legs
Lipolymphedema cause: functional venous insufficiency with insufficient venous pump activity
Treatment for lipolymphedema: compression stockings for years
Family history: similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt
Father's cause of death: intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography result: intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations with a maximum diameter of 1.2 cm

Histopathology result: well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis of the epidermis overlying a conglomerate of dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle in the upper dermis, partly showing thrombosis
Genetic testing result: detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant
Demographics: female patient in her late 20s
Chief complaint: 2-year history of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Location of patches and plaques: left upper arm to the left side of her chest
Symptoms: occasional slight pain
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
Denied fever, weight loss, or fatigue
Multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders on her left axilla, medial upper arm, and lateral thoracic region
No extracutaneous involvement was observed
Histopathological examination: thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results: positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results: negative for podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

Demographics: teenage girl
Chief complaint: several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
Chief complaint: several weeks of external deviation of her nasal septum
Past medical history: no significant past medical history mentioned
Physical examination finding: left nasal mass
Physical examination finding: mild left-sided proptosis
Imaging study: CT scan (without and with contrast) of the left maxillary sinus
Image Title: Computed tomographic scans of a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Computed tomographic scans of a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Imaging finding: heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components completely opacifying the left maxillary sinus
Imaging finding: mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
Imaging finding: no extension beyond cribriform plate
Imaging finding: displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
Imaging finding: left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved
Imaging finding: bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
Biopsy result: tissue analysis showed spindle cell process in a patternless arrangement with significant multinucleated giant cells
Biopsy result: rare mitotic activity
Biopsy result: no cytologic atypia
Biopsy result: largest portion measured 7.0 × 4.0 × 2.0 cm
Demographics: 11-year-old boy
Chief complaint: progressive unilateral skin hardening on right thigh and buttock for 7 years
Limited motion of right limb joint
Ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving right thigh above the patella extending to right buttocks
Loss of skin elasticity
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of right thigh demonstrated slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Normal epidermis and mild pigmentation along the basal layer with subtle increase in density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment but no evidence of inflammation
Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Alcian blue staining: Negative
MRI of right thigh
Demographics: 59-year-old woman
Chief complaint: 2 days of left orbital pain
Medical history: hypertension controlled with lisinopril
Medical history: several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/400 OS
Edematous, hyperemic left eyelids
Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Normal intraocular pressure
Normal fundi on both sides
Imaging: Coronal Computed Tomography Scan showed left-sided lacrimal sac abscess
Imaging: postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Imaging: minimal sinus mucosal thickening
Imaging: opacification of both nasolacrimal ducts
Imaging: Repeat Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography showed increased abscess size with globe compression
Imaging: minimal intraconal fat stranding
Imaging: unremarkable optic nerve appearance on follow-up CT
Imaging: Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Angiography showed patent ophthalmic artery
Imaging: diffusion-weighted imaging showed acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve
Laboratory: Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains
Laboratory: later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes
